long_biography.plain_text:
Leipold established Ameritel in Wisconsin and served as president of the business-services company. He later became chairman and chief executive of LaCrosse-Rainfair Safety Company, a maker of protective clothing and footwear. These positions document an entrepreneurial record independent of the companies and inherited wealth associated with his spouse's family.

Professional hockey became his central focus when he secured Nashville's expansion club. After a decade as chairman and governor, he transferred the Predators and arena-operating business to a local group in 2007. NHL governors approved his acquisition of Minnesota Sports & Entertainment in 2008. Today he directs that organisation's commercial operations and represents the Wild at league board meetings. Its remit also covers an American Hockey League affiliate, venue management and other entertainment businesses.
